notes: V4 matrix spec is already locked and should be treated as closed input, not active design work.
Implementation-readiness artifacts say only live control-plane actions remain: import bundles into Convex, register packages, create experiments, and optionally launch canaries.
Infra hardening is complete: Temporal-owned Media Cloud acquisition is live, Railway worker bootstrap is simplified, and the latest live acquisition smoke passed.
The remaining mission is a launch-and-monitor loop, which is exactly the kind of repeated bounded execution a workspace should own.

current.summary: The repo has a locked V4 spec, live-ready runtime, local target bundles, and canary tooling. What remains is the live execution campaign: import, package registration, experiment creation, canary promotion, and monitored launch.

workflowRuns.requestedObjective: Compile the first bounded V4 launch workflow: live import Gilardi and Zheng assets into Convex, register paper-audit packages, create the first canary experiments, define the monitoring/debug ladder, and specify promotion gates from canary to full matrix execution.
Instantiate the locked V4 headline matrix, launch the first cohort cells across the provider panel, and apply the monitored promotion/prune loop at matrix scale.

Launch the remaining locked headline conditions after the baseline cohort: cross-provider abstention and Gilardi `l2_neutralized`, using the hardened tag policy and the same monitored promotion/prune loop.

Analyze the first clean pass of the full 20-cell V4 headline matrix, summarize the most important geometry/provider findings, and define the monitored rerun or promotion policy for follow-on launch work.
Execute the GPT-4.1-only targeted rerun cohort for V4: rerun Gilardi baseline and l2 plus Zheng baseline and abstention, then compare the reruns against the first-pass outputs.

bottlenecks: The Zheng single-turn GPT-4.1 baseline experiment row contains two completed runs because the initial canary tag matched the baseline tag before the tag policy was hardened.
The current abstention contract remains weak on this matrix, and the GPT-4.1 rerun does not rescue it as a stable effect.
The next campaign step is no longer more reruns by default; it is deciding how to write up the weak-abstention result and whether any appendix translated-prompt work is worth the budget.

decisions.statement: Use a dedicated V4 launch workspace instead of extending the closed spec or readiness workspaces, because the remaining work is repeated live execution and promotion/prune control.
Treat the existing runtime as sufficient; only pursue more runtime changes when a real canary exposes a bounded blocker.
Start with Gilardi and Zheng baseline canaries before any broader headline cohort launch.
After the live launch-tool fix, Gilardi, Zheng single-turn, and Zheng multi-turn baseline canaries all completed with zero failures; the next campaign step is full matrix instantiation.

The first full baseline provider cohort completed with zero failures across Gilardi and Zheng. Tag conflicts must now hard-fail, and Zheng canary tags were renamed to avoid reuse of headline experiment rows.
Semantic-view launch cohorts must verify transform coverage before live start. The Gilardi l2 cohort only launched after a targeted transform run generated full `l2_neutralized` coverage.

The full 20-cell headline matrix has now completed one clean pass. Mild provider formatting drift in freeform label tasks should be handled by parser recovery rather than treated as a launch-stopping failure.

First-pass analysis shows zero observed abstains across 392 responses and zero Zheng baseline ties across all four providers. The most important movement is the Gilardi raw-vs-l2 contrast, especially on Claude Sonnet 4.

The GPT-4.1 rerun cohort stabilizes the main interpretation: Gilardi baseline is exact-repeat stable, Zheng abstention is exact-repeat stable, and the only remaining movement is one borderline Gilardi l2 item and one tie-adjacent Zheng baseline item.
